messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Recap + Next Steps: Reliability & graceful degradation discussion (FinServX)

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the time earlier — appreciated the candid discussion about recent incidents and your reliability goals. Quick written recap so we’re aligned and to capture immediate next steps.

Key takeaways (pain points)
- Recent production incidents (2–3 in the last 6 months) caused user-facing regressions when regional capacity dropped and fallback paths didn’t preserve output quality.
- Primary failure modes you called out: GPU OOMs on peak traffic, cache invalidation spikes, and delayed fallbacks that increased tail-latency.
- Current stack: in-house proxy (LLMProxy), model variants (large model primary, smaller quantized model for fallback), and downstream reranker.

Stated success criteria
- SLA: availability you want in the mid 99.9s (you mentioned target >= 99.95%).
- Latency SLO: keep P95 under ~350ms for critical inference routes (with graceful degradation for P99 spikes).
- Seamless graceful degradation: automated fallback to compatible model variant/region without loss of critical fields or hallucination increase.
- Cost-awareness: keep per-token spend within targets you provided (we noted your cost ceiling during the call).

What Redwood can help with (high level)
- Canary rollout + regional fallback policy that triggers model/region switch before user-impacting errors.
- Prefix/KV caching and batch tuning to reduce OOM frequency and tail latency.
- Quantized fallback models tested against your reranker to measure quality delta.
- Playbook for incident handling: observability hooks, automatic rollbacks, and transparent tracing for post-incident RCA.

Immediate next steps (agreed)
1) I’ll share a 1-page pilot plan and short benchmark sheet by EOD tomorrow (attached: postcall-recap PDF).
2) Elena: share the incident timeline spreadsheet and any recent logs you can lawfully provide (we discussed redacting PII).
3) Schedule a follow-up workshop (technical) with your infra and our reliability engineer — proposed slots: Tue 17 Feb 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 18 Feb 14:00–15:00 PT.
4) We’ll prepare two fallback options to validate: regional failover to secondary cluster, and in-region fallback to a quantized model variant with pre-warmed KV cache.

If I missed anything, flag it here and I’ll update the recap. Looking forward to the workshop.

Thanks,

--
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Aditya —

Thanks for the thorough recap. This looks accurate. A few clarifications from our side:

Incident history summary (to confirm)
- We logged 3 incidents in the last 6 months that had customer impact: two were GPU OOMs during batch processing spikes and one was a control-plane bug that cleared caches unexpectedly.
- When the primary cluster dropped, our current fallback (smaller quantized model) produced higher latency and lower downstream NDCG; the system routed traffic to a different region which introduced tokenization/version mismatches.

Additional constraints
- We must preserve certain output fields (policy IDs and account flags) during any fallback — even if other outputs degrade.
- All test artifacts must remain behind our VPC for compliance during pilot (we can provide a temporary peered test VPC).

Attachments: I attached the incident-timeline CSV and a small anonymized log excerpt.

Workshop: Tue 17 Feb 10:00 PT works for us. Please send a calendar invite.

One more ask: would you include a short checklist of what Infra needs to provide ahead of the workshop (network peering, sample payloads, expected QPS/peak profiles)? That will help us come prepared.

Elena
Director, Platform Reliability
FinServX
